thread.title: Caterpillar Earnings Miss Badly; Caterpillar Stock Falls, Dow Jones Retreats

author: JED GRAHAM
title: Caterpillar Earnings Miss Badly; Caterpillar Stock Falls, Dow Jones Retreats
text:
Dow Jones industrial average component Caterpillar ( CAT ), a bellwether for the global economy, reported earnings early Monday that missed Wall Street expectations. Caterpillar stock, which has been trying to break out of bear market territory, fell on the report, weighing on the Dow Jones.
X Caterpillar kicked off a big earnings week for the Dow Jones . Apple ( AAPL ) is set to report, as are a trio of leading Dow stocks: Boeing ( BA ), Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Visa ( V ).
Caterpillar Earnings Estimates: Analysts expected Caterpillar earnings per share to expand 38% to $2.98 in the fourth quarter on revenue growth of 11% to $14.37 billion.
Results: Caterpillar earnings rose 18% to $2.55 a share. Revenue climbed 11% to $14.34 billion.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Outlook: The construction equipment giant provided 2019 guidance for adjusted EPS of $11.75 to $12.75. Prior to Caterpillar's fourth-quarter results, analysts expected Caterpillar earnings of $12.64 for the coming year, according to Zacks Investment Research.
"Our outlook assumes a modest sales increase based on the fundamentals of our diverse end markets as well as the macroeconomic and geopolitical environment," Caterpillar said.
Caterpillar Stock Shares of the Dow Jones component sank 9.1% to close at 124.37 after Monday's earnings report. Caterpillar stock rose 3.1% to 136.86 on Friday, ahead of earnings, hitting its highest close since December 3. But Caterpillar stock was still 21% below its all-time high of 173.24 hit in January 2018.
Caterpillar stock nearly tripled over two years after bottoming in January 2016, riding a global economic rebound that crested by early 2018. The softer global economy, led by a downshift in China, has weighed on industrial commodity prices and moderated expectations for Caterpillar's resource industry revival.
Caterpillar has been a victim of President Trump's trade war, facing higher commodity costs due to tariffs on steel and aluminum imports. Meanwhile, the China slowdown has been exacerbated by worry over Trump tariffs, leading to something of a backlash against U.S. multinationals. That seemed to partly explain the recent big revenue miss from Apple on weak iPhone sales.
The bull case for Caterpillar starts with a China trade deal and major stimulus from Beijing that helps lift the Chinese economy out of its funk in a repeat of 2016.
